fullPassage:
Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation. Who would you like to have as your listener?
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.
Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a (A)[presentation / preservation] in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are (B)[holding / folding] under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her (C)[homework / housework].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 수업 시간에 발표를 하고 있다고 상상하라. 학생들이 책상 아래 무언가를 들고 있고, 다른 학생은 숙제를 하는 것 같다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① presentation — holding — homework
❌ ② preservation — holding — housework
❌ ③ presentation — folding — housework
❌ ④ preservation — folding — homework
✅ (A) presentation: '발표'가 수업 맥락에 적합. preservation(보존)은 무관. ✅ (B) holding: '들고 있다'. folding(접다)은 문맥 부적합. ✅ (C) homework: '숙제'. housework(집안일)는 학교 맥락에 부적합.
det.tip: presentation(발표) vs preservation(보존). homework(숙제) vs housework(집안일).

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication (A)[climate / conflict]. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that (B)[interests / interrupts] you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some (C)[techniques / theories] that will be useful when it is your time to speak.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 좋은 청자는 긍정적인 소통 분위기를 만들어 줄 수 있다. 발표에서 흥미로운 것을 찾아야 하고, 유용한 기법을 습득할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① conflict — interests — theories
❌ ② climate — interrupts — techniques
✅ ③ climate — interests — techniques
❌ ④ conflict — interrupts — theories
✅ (A) climate: 'communication climate'(소통 분위기). conflict(갈등)는 positive와 모순. ✅ (B) interests: '흥미를 끈다'. interrupts(방해한다)는 맥락 부적합. ✅ (C) techniques: '기법/기술'. theories(이론)는 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: communication climate = 소통 분위기. pick up techniques = 기법을 습득하다.

questions.passage: When you discuss or (A)[evaluate / eliminate] others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an (B)[attitude / altitude] you will appreciate when others comment on your speech. Listening well is as (C)[important / imposing] as speaking well.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 다른 사람의 발표를 토론하거나 평가할 때, 건설적이고 도움이 되어야 한다. 그것은 감사할 태도이다. 잘 듣는 것은 잘 말하는 것만큼 중요하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① eliminate — attitude — imposing
✅ ② evaluate — attitude — important
❌ ③ evaluate — altitude — imposing
❌ ④ eliminate — altitude — important
✅ (A) evaluate: '평가하다'. eliminate(제거하다)는 맥락 부적합. ✅ (B) attitude: '태도'. altitude(고도)는 무관. ✅ (C) important: '중요한'. imposing(인상적인)은 as~as 비교 맥락에 부적합.
det.tip: evaluate(평가하다) vs eliminate(제거하다). attitude(태도) vs altitude(고도).

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is ①<u>texting</u> on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are ②<u>laughing</u> over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a ③<u>supportive</u> look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your ④<u>resignation</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ resignation(사직서)이 아니라 presentation(발표)이 맞다. 수업 시간에 사직서를 줄 리가 없다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①texting(문자하다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②laughing(웃다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③supportive(지지하는): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④resignation(사직서): 원문은 presentation(발표). 수업 맥락에서 사직서는 부적절.
det.tip: presentation(발표) vs resignation(사직). 학교 수업 맥락에서 발표가 적절.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a ①<u>positive</u> communication climate. As a listener, you should listen ②<u>carelessly</u> and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be ③<u>useful</u> when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be ④<u>constructive</u> and helpful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② carelessly(부주의하게)가 아니라 carefully(주의 깊게)가 맞다. 좋은 청자는 주의 깊게 들어야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①positive(긍정적인): 원문 그대로. ❌ ②carelessly(부주의하게): 원문은 carefully(주의 깊게). 좋은 청자 맥락에서 부주의하게는 모순. ✅ ③useful(유용한): 원문 그대로. ✅ ④constructive(건설적인): 원문 그대로.
det.tip: carefully(주의 깊게) ↔ carelessly(부주의하게). 청자의 태도 맥락에서 주의 깊게가 적절.

questions.passage: That is an attitude you will appreciate when others ①<u>comment</u> on your speech. Listening well is as ②<u>important</u> as speaking well. ③<u>Fortunately</u>, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to ④<u>ignore</u> you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ ignore(무시하다)가 아니라 listen to(귀 기울이다)가 맞다. 황금률은 '네가 대접받고 싶은 대로 남을 대접하라'는 뜻이므로 '들어주길 원하는 대로 들어라'이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①comment(논평하다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②important(중요한): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③Fortunately(다행히): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④ignore(무시하다): 원문은 listen to(들어주다). 경청의 황금률에서 무시하라는 것은 정반대.
det.tip: listen to(귀 기울이다) ↔ ignore(무시하다). Golden Rule은 상대를 대접하라는 원칙.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a __________ look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 들을 준비가 된 학생의 표정은 지지하는(supportive) 표정이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③supportive(지지하는): 원문 'a supportive look on his face'. ❌ ①hostile(적대적인): 들을 준비와 모순. ❌ ②indifferent(무관심한): 들을 준비와 모순. ❌ ④confused(혼란스러운): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: supportive = 지지하는, 격려하는. ready to listen + supportive look = 적극적 청자.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be __________ and helpful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다른 사람의 발표를 토론하거나 평가할 때, 건설적이고(constructive) 도움이 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①constructive(건설적인): 원문 'be constructive and helpful'. ❌ ②destructive(파괴적인): helpful과 모순. ❌ ③competitive(경쟁적인): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④repetitive(반복적인): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: constructive(건설적인) ↔ destructive(파괴적인). be constructive and helpful = 건설적이고 도움이 되게.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some __________ that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주제에 관심이 없더라도, 나중에 유용할 기법(techniques)을 습득할 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②techniques(기법): 원문 'pick up some techniques that will be useful'. ❌ ①obstacles(장애물): useful과 모순. ❌ ③complaints(불만): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④assumptions(가정): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: pick up techniques = 기법/기술을 습득하다. useful과 자연스럽게 연결.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication <u>climate</u>. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'climate'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: communication climate = 소통 분위기. climate는 여기서 '기후'가 아니라 '분위기(atmosphere)'를 뜻한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④atmosphere(분위기): 소통 분위기라는 비유적 의미. ❌ ①weather(날씨): 문자적 의미. ❌ ②challenge(도전): 무관. ❌ ③structure(구조): 무관.
det.tip: climate: (1)기후 (2)분위기/풍토. communication climate = 소통 분위기 = atmosphere.

questions.passage: When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will <u>appreciate</u> when others comment on your speech.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'appreciate'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: appreciate = 감사하다, 높이 평가하다 = value(가치 있게 여기다).
det.analysis: ✅ ②value(가치 있게 여기다): appreciate의 동의어. ❌ ①criticize(비판하다): 반의어. ❌ ③ignore(무시하다): 반의어. ❌ ④memorize(외우다): 무관.
det.tip: appreciate = (1)감사하다 (2)가치를 알다/높이 평가하다. value와 동의.

questions.passage: Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may <u>pick up</u> some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'pick up'과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: pick up = (자연스럽게) 습득하다/배우다 = learn.
det.analysis: ✅ ①learn(배우다): pick up의 동의어(자연스러운 습득). ❌ ②discard(버리다): 반대. ❌ ③display(보여주다): 무관. ❌ ④postpone(연기하다): 무관.
det.tip: pick up: (1)줍다 (2)습득하다. 여기서는 '기법을 자연스럽게 배우다' 의미.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a <u>positive</u> communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'positive'와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: positive(긍정적인) ↔ negative(부정적인).
det.analysis: ✅ ③negative(부정적인): positive의 정반대. ❌ ①active(활동적인): 유사 맥락이지만 반의어 아님. ❌ ②practical(실용적인): 무관. ❌ ④neutral(중립적인): 반대가 아니라 중간.
det.tip: positive(긍정적인) ↔ negative(부정적인). 가장 대표적인 반의어 쌍.

questions.passage: When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be <u>constructive</u> and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'constructive'와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: constructive(건설적인) ↔ destructive(파괴적인).
det.analysis: ✅ ①destructive(파괴적인): constructive의 정반대. ❌ ②productive(생산적인): 유사한 긍정 의미. ❌ ③instructive(교육적인): 유사한 긍정 의미. ❌ ④protective(보호하는): 무관.
det.tip: constructive(건설적인) ↔ destructive(파괴적인). construct(건설하다) ↔ destruct(파괴하다).

questions.passage:
(A) Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to <u>speak</u>.

(B) When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful.
questions.stem: (A)의 'speak'와 (B)의 'speeches'의 의미를 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?

det.korean: (A) 유용한 기법을 나중에 발표할 때 쓸 수 있다. (B) 다른 사람들의 발표/연설을 평가할 때.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 언어를 구사하다 — (B) 연설문
✅ ② (A) 발표하다 — (B) 발표/연설
❌ ③ (A) 대화하다 — (B) 대화
❌ ④ (A) 발표하다 — (B) 언어 능력
✅ ② (A)발표하다: 'your time to speak'에서 청중 앞에서 발표하는 의미. (B)발표/연설: 'others' speeches'에서 다른 사람의 발표물.
det.tip: speak: (1)말하다 (2)발표하다. speech: (1)연설/발표 (2)언어능력 (3)말투.

questions.stem:
다음 영어 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to judge or determine the quality, importance, or value of something"

det.korean: 어떤 것의 품질, 중요성, 가치를 판단하다 = evaluate(평가하다).
det.analysis: ✅ ②evaluate(평가하다): 정의와 정확히 일치. ❌ ①eliminate(제거하다): 판단이 아닌 제거. ❌ ③elaborate(자세히 설명하다): 판단이 아닌 설명. ❌ ④emigrate(이민 가다): 완전히 다른 의미.
det.tip: evaluate = 평가하다. e(밖으로) + value(가치) + ate(동사) = 가치를 매기다.

questions.passage:
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.

Listening well is as important as speaking well. [fortune], anyone can become a better listener.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 [fortune]을 문맥에 맞게 올바른 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 다행히도 = Fortunately. 문장 부사로 사용되어 문장 전체를 수식한다.
det.analysis: ✅ Fortunately: fortune(행운) → fortunate(운 좋은) → fortunately(다행히). 문장 부사로 쉼표 앞에 위치.
det.tip: fortune(명사: 행운) → fortunate(형용사: 운 좋은) → fortunately(부사: 다행히도). 문장 부사는 문장 앞에 위치.

questions.passage:
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.

Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of [listen]: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 [listen]을 문맥에 맞게 올바른 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 경청의 황금률 = the Golden Rule of Listening. 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사.
det.analysis: ✅ Listening: 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사(V-ing) 형태. 'the Golden Rule of Listening'은 고유명사처럼 쓰인 표현.
det.tip: 전치사 + 동명사(V-ing). of listening = 듣기의/경청의. 전치사 뒤에는 명사/동명사만 가능.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to __________. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 발표자에게 지지하는 표정으로 발표를 기다리는 학생 = 들을(listen) 준비가 된 학생.
det.analysis: ✅ ②listen(듣다): 원문 'ready to listen'. 지지하는 표정과 기다림이 단서. ❌ ①leave(떠나다): 맥락 반대. ❌ ③complain(불평하다): supportive와 모순. ❌ ④perform(공연하다): 청자 역할과 불일치.
det.tip: ready to listen = 들을 준비가 된. supportive look + waiting = 적극적 경청 자세.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will __________ when others comment on your speech.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 건설적이고 도움이 되는 태도는 다른 사람이 당신의 발표를 평할 때 감사히 여길(appreciate) 태도이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④appreciate(감사하다): 원문 'you will appreciate'. 건설적 태도를 남이 자기에게 해주면 고마울 것이라는 논리. ❌ ①reject(거부하다): 맥락 반대. ❌ ②overlook(간과하다): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ③exaggerate(과장하다): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: appreciate = 감사하다/가치를 알다. 건설적 태도 → 남에게 받으면 고마운 태도.
